items.place: Aral Sea, east basin of the Large Aral (Uzbekistan/Kazakhstan)
items.what_changed: In July 1997 smooth open water covers the western two-thirds of the box up to a sharp eastern shore; in October 2026 the same area shows land texture everywhere, with the long island's outline now sitting in dry seabed and a straight track crossing where the water was.
items.band_note: RADARSAT-1 is C-band (5.6 cm wavelength), NISAR is L-band (24 cm): L-band sees deeper into vegetation and dry soil, so brightness differences are partly the sensor, not the ground. Water stays dark in both.

items.place: Lake Urmia, north-central lake and causeway (Iran)
items.what_changed: The island and the causeway line are the same in both; in 1999 dark water ends at a sharp eastern shore, while in 2026 the dark area runs past that old shore, and dark L-band can be water or a smooth dry salt bed, so these two radar images alone do not show how much water is left.
